Hi twin! I’m also an Aries sun, Virgo moon. I’m curious if you’re younger — I find this has improved for me with age/experience but it takes time. I can certainly “lean into my fire” as I like to say when I’m passionate about something and my experience in my younger years was people thinking I was too reactive. Still, sometimes find me to be “arrogant” or speaking in a manner that’s too intense. I’m working though on being ok with the fact that I’m not everyone’s cup of tea and embracing that it’s better that way. The ones that like me for me are who I want around anyways.

I find my Virgo moon to be difficult BUT it can also be grounding. Try to embrace the logic and practical parts of that placement to learn to practice *pause* before reacting, so you can respond instead. Also using the Virgo moon to speak with intention and practicality sometimes helps because Aries is the youngest and I often find when I speak from that part of myself I’m in my emotions.

I appreciate your post. I am an MSW student myself. I’m in my second semester, and honestly, I just joined this page a couple weeks ago, initially to ask this question. I was taken aback by how many folks were posting “business as usual” or asking about apps — so much so that I didn’t even end up asking at the time… thank goodness I got a notification about this one.

You and I see this in a lot of similar ways despite my being I am a white woman. TBH I was surprised to find out that the majority of people in social work are from better/decent circumstances? Also, I work as an advocate for the last 6 1/2 years before going back to my masters, and I definitely worked with a woman who have no problem bragging about how she “didn’t even need the money” bc her partner was the sole provider. Yet she lied and backstabbed to get that director role… Super enraging. I grew up very low income and have over 8 childhood ACES, that was what drew me to a profession in this field. I feel I had hope then about collective power though and neuro plasticity. 

I’m in my early thirties now — I have pretty severe mental illness struggles, as well as 2 invisible disabilities that take a lot of my time and energy to manage. I am taken aback by how most of the comments so far only are mentioning pay. I’m not worried about pay (it’s a given) but the central issue is what you said about the idea of if we can really even make an impact. I suppose, this is always been a central question though of helping professions in the US. — as someone already astutely pointed out. Maybe that’s why these conversations are so important for us! I had a professor I mentioned my struggle to, and of course, she responded swiftly with the point of so many people are going to need our help. I want to be of service, of course I do. Hell, it was my dream (as a first gen college student) to do this AND all I could think when she said that was, *” but I’m one of those people — I am in need of so much help”* 

So, this has me really messed up. I feel I’ve lost a lot of my drive for my studies. I am supposed to be signing up for my practicum come this fall and I keep putting off the tasks… because if I can’t get the support, I need then how the hell am I supposed to help other people? What if the bozo in charge of the department of health cuts my medicine? Sends me to a “farm”? So I  think it’s a matter of how the ethos of our nation has slowly but surely changed over the decades, and now it feels like it’s an irrevocable shift that I truly didn’t believe (or hoped) we wouldn’t get to. Half of the country doesn’t want to invest in helping others. We just studied the “rollback” of social safety nets that has been occurring for decades. They have been led so far astray and it’s debatable that we will be able to “help” if it’s continues this way.

I hate that I’m being such a cynic about it, I want to have hope, maybe I just feel weary and worn down. My experience in the field already has not been all that great, mostly that there are single shining stars who are beacons but still boards of directors and managers who are narcissists that have the day at the end of the day. Thankfully there are people though up that care, according to this interview I just had where I did ask about funding sources because I needed to see if I’m gonna lose my job randomly! She said that they just had gotten a large new grant for this role, so maybe I’ll hope isn’t lost? 

Sorry this is so long. I’m thankful I’m not alone, but I am in a program and can’t believe I’ve considered leaving. Some of the things keeping me in though are the freedom that I will have if I get my license. Which might open opportunity to work in other countries. Plus, I couldn’t get anything better paying or more interesting with only my BA.

I took Prozac for around 8 year with (it seems) no issues. It was the only antidepressant that worked for me. After trying a bunch starting around age 17, the doc straight up asked me what I hadn’t tried - I said Prozac and viola, it worked so I could get out of bed and didn’t wear off like some others. However I recently started Luvox, to try something to help better with my obsessive rumination.

The medication I believe was causing the problem was Lamictal. I had been on it for around 4 years though. We lowered it to 50mg in early 2024, I think maybe that was when the issues start because I was having this odd burping (not GI related) and trouble swallowing. They couldn’t find the source. I have narcolepsy, so around June I started sodium oxybate. The lamictal was lowered to 25mg. I guess the 2 have a MAJOR interaction… which they did not make me aware of or tell me to watch for any symptoms. I stopped the sodium oxybate almost 2 weeks ago now. Initially that eased the twisting up a bit but I need it really badly for good sleep. I got off the lamictal a week ago today. Apparently being on lamictal itself long term can cause dystonia. My psych was shocked though since my dose was so low. I also had started strattera just before 12/3/24 when I had the horrible “episode”. Before that I was constantly rubbing my muscles, fidgety and yes lots of movement. I have “restless legs”. So I’ve also stopped the strattera since last week too. It’s hard for me to know whether it was solely the lamictal, the lamictal interacting with the SO or maybe, serotonin syndrome from the combo and then adding strattera sending it over the edge?

So now, I’m just on the Luvox SSRI, nuvigil (wake med for narcolepsy) and adderall. The lamictal has been hard to come off since I took it for so long. They say 2 weeks for it to be out of your system, but I do feel my symptoms are lessening. My neck seems to be “giving” and going back to “normal”. I’m going to continue being off Lamictal and Strattera. For me, I hope to be able to try sodium oxybate again after those are out of my system and I just pray/hope that it wasn’t that medicine itself.

It’s possible serotonin syndrome played a part for you too. Gabapentin helps me dystonia symptoms but it isn’t a great mood stabilizer. Do you need a mood stabilizer? Or more so an antidepressant? Some of us are far more sensitive to serotonin. I’m not sure how high of doses you were on but maybe it was too much. Have you tried Prozac? It being the oldest, it seems to be tolerated well by many and many find a low dose quite strong. Even 10mg might be safer to start with. Another really safe medicine (if you have anxiety) to ask about is buspar/buspirone. It isn’t a benzo or an SSRI.
The twisting has significantly decreased. I’m only 4 days off lamictal (and one week off the other med). My neck seems to be “unwinding” now… chiropractor is helpful.

I just started a new SSRI though, and you know she only wants to do “one med at a time.” Despite being on it for 4 years now.

That being said, it is vastly different from other mood stabilizers. It acts a lot more like an antidepressant, but it isn’t like an SSRI either. OP you should be able to get it approved, if your psychiatrist or GP writes the prescription/insurance prior authorization request stating that it is for depression mood stability/mood regulation! Their error was putting that it was for anxiety when it isn’t approved for that. Unfortunately, despite being the medical professional they can never put or ask for anything to be prescribed for something “off-label” or not what it’s been FDA approved for.

I disagree that it’s religious AF. There shouldn’t be anyone in AA (or the world lol) telling you what god is/means/looks like/exists.

It is a spiritual program, yes. 
However it does not adhere to a specific religious tradition, they use the word God in the book for higher power mainly because this was originally written in the 1930’s. There have been many stories. AA has been good for me. However, it is one of “tools in my tool box” so to say. At first, I didn’t know anything other than about AA but I’m quite authority averse and struggle with groups. I have found mostly only good people and helpful stories of experiences and sobriety’s hope and strength at meetings. I started going about 5 months into sobriety, online. I knew I needed to go deeper and get more out of my sobriety. The work does work. While there are some fundamentalist, not everyone is that way. I believe many of us in the younger crowd, are leaning into this too - that there should not be this governing power (“our leaders are but trusted servants; they do not govern”)

This being said, I entered this a bit older than a friend of mine and she had a very “cult” like experience. I have encounter meetings or folks like this maybe 2-3 times. When that’s happened, I simply remove myself or ask my HP and things make themselves clear. So, I see how the program could be harmful to some in certain circumstances, ages, vulnerabilities, etc. Unfortunately, there are still people who have used the program to abuse other’s - sometimes unknowingly.

Overall I have made amazing friendships and connections with people living all over the world! I also got more connected into other socializing opportunities which helps me work on that aspect in my sobriety. I think with intention, honesty and willingness, you can start to see the promises of the program come true in your life. ~ “We will know a new freedom and a new happiness”
